### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **92** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`, `os lint (command, 45 pages)`, `/automation/:name (route, 48 pages)`, `/meta/:type (route, 40 pages)`, `/meta/:type/:name (route, 43 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa5e0181198a1910c01102fa4075ef0256e09a6d` — the merge of head `7cfcbc304fb950914fa0acfffa3b486231577322` into base `9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa5e0181198a1910c01102fa4075ef0256e09a6d && git checkout fa5e0181198a1910c01102fa4075ef0256e09a6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33 7cfcbc304fb950914fa0acfffa3b486231577322 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33 && git merge --no-ff 7cfcbc304fb950914fa0acfffa3b486231577322

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9e1f1f90d5a62c81b6d1561d4baa7c822cc88b33` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7cfcbc304fb950914fa0acfffa3b486231577322`
Local-runs: probe — one independent FNV-1a 32 computation (a 6-line python function outside the repo tree, no repo code, no build, no test, no gate) of the test's pinned vector and the three published vectors, to judge the dev-flagged Acceptance note 1: the green check-runs prove the pin is self-consistent with the implementation, not that the implementation is FNV-1a.
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/face-name.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/endpoint.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/index.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.bucket-two-three-name-underscore-led-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/security/sharing.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts, skills/README.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json + packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts (the gate that enforces D9's retirement and the sentence SKILL.md teaches about it), packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts (docblocks only; they describe lint.ts), .changeset/31669-behavioural-names-short-address-grammar.md (judged in ②), content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx (prose face the round made false). Lane remainder at TIER_DEFAULT, not reviewed here: the 12 test files and the dogfood fixture, the 7 regenerated spec surface artefacts, the 2 regenerated reference pages, the regenerated audit count. Read in the live tree to judge, never reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` (ROUTE_LEDGER), `shared/identifiers.zod.ts`, `kernel/customization-package.ts`, `meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts`, `cli/src/utils/project-namespace.ts`, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`, the FNV-1a sites in service-settings, service-messaging, types, metadata-core and platform-objects, `packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/skills/package.json`.

Inputs: card #31669 body and all 8 comments (triage 6727644402, claim 6727701819 and amends 6727833678 / 6727964762 / 6730426080, devx notifies 6730710213 / 6731365836, dev report 6731284162); PR #31765 body, 48-file list, net diff `origin/main...7cfcbc30` (base 9e1f1f90); the 67 check-runs on the head (57 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed; the skipped ones are opt-in or matrix-template jobs; combined status `pending` carries no contexts); the five ruling records on #31527 (6723462584, 6723499113, 6723571682, 6724050556, 6724530715); ADR-0150 at the head (e81636ce, #31676's amendment included).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies:

1. **Ten name schemas narrow** from `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` to `ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN` `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` with `ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_MESSAGE`: tool, skill, agent, flow, hook, connector (both `ConnectorSchema` and `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`, which share `connectorBaseShape`), sharing rule (via `BaseSharingRuleSchema`), job, cube, api endpoint. **Right.** ADR-0150 D5 names exactly these ten as the ones that admitted a leading `_`; I verified on `main` that every other bucket 2/3 name is `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (action, webhook, mapping, assignment rule, queue, app, page, dashboard, report, dataset, permission set, picklist, position), whose regex is the same `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, so the narrowing is exactly the card's declared one and nothing beyond it. It binds environment rows too, as D5 says ("bucket 4 included"). Letter-led names, prefixed or short, parse byte-identically (the regex differs only in the first class). The PR touches no other accepted value.
2. **`manifest.namespace` reads `NAMESPACE_PATTERN`** — the same regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$` and the same message as before; `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` reads the same constant in place of its private twin. Accept-set unchanged. **Right.**
3. **`McpActionNamespaceSchema` / `McpListedActionAddressSchema` / `MCP_ACTION_NAMESPACE_MEMBER`** — additive declarations, wired to nothing (`packages/mcp` untouched, confirmed on the file list). The namespace value is bound to the manifest grammar, so a value the tool admits is one a manifest can declare (D2: the address is the namespace). The listed-row schema is a non-strict `z.object`, deliberately: it is a mix-in for a row that carries the server's own members (label, params, confirmation), as the docblock says; the `ai/` strictness count regenerated 91 → 92 and the ledger gate is green. `name` is a plain string on the row because the row is server-produced. **Right.**
4. **`findNamespaceObjectNameClashes`** — additive, unwired (the card says K wires the doors). Both directions are judged; the `NS_custom` corollary reads `CUSTOMIZATION_NAMESPACE_SUFFIX` (`'_custom'` on `main`) rather than a second literal; each clash names both spellings and the package when known. **Right**, matches ruling 6724530715 and the ADR K row.
5. **`NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS` values** — measured by hand against `ROUTE_LEDGER` at 9e1f1f90: `/automation` → `_status` (L618), `actions` (L595), `connectors` (L596), `hooks` (L656), `trigger` (L589); `/actions` → the empty segment (L746 `POST /actions//:action`), `_activation` (L748), `global` (L737); `/automation/connectors` → `credential-refs` (L600–604), `oauth` (L616); `/automation/trigger`, `/automation/hooks` and `/meta/:type` serve no literal at the namespace position (`_drafts`, `_migrate-stored`, `types`, `object` sit in the type position). Complete, nothing extra, code-unit order. `NAMESPACE_REFUSED_LITERALS` = `actions, connectors, global, hooks, oauth, trigger` follows (the `_`-led, the empty and the hyphenated literal fail the grammar). **Right.**
6. **`os lint` `naming/namespace-prefix`**: the bare-name finding now fires only for `capabilities` and `positions`. Both are keys of `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (L83, L76 on `main`), so the finding is live, not dead; every other collection is silent; the duplicate finding is unchanged over `DUPLICATE_KEYED_TYPES` (apps, pages, dashboards, flows, actions by `objectName:name`, reports, datasets), which is exactly the list SKILL.md's new sentence teaches. The `overrides`, namespace-named, `sys_`, dotted, no-namespace and `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES` exemptions are preserved on the two judged collections. **Right** against D9 ("retired by child P: phase 2's bare-name warning for buckets 2–4; the intra-package duplicate warning stays") and D1/D7 for what still keeps the prefix.

Public-surface changes:

7. `@objectstack/spec/kernel` gains 8 value exports and 4 types; `@objectstack/spec/ai` gains `deriveAiFaceName`, 4 constants, `AiFaceAddress`, and the 3 MCP members with their types. Every one is named in the changeset; `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `authorable-surface` and `json-schema.manifest` are regenerated and `check:generated`/`check:api-surface` are inside the green Lint & Repo Gates run. **Right.**
8. `@objectstack/cli`: `NAME_JUDGED_ELSEWHERE` retired, `PREFIX_JUDGED_COLLECTIONS` added. `commands/lint` is not a package subpath (`exports`: `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`) and no file outside `packages/cli` references the old name, so this is not a published removal and the changeset rightly does not list it. **Right.**
9. The card's "namespace on MCP `run_action` / `list_actions` shapes" is satisfied in spec only; the tool input and row shape live in `packages/mcp`. Claim amend 1 corrected that premise before the build and the ADR's G2 row owns the mcp wiring. **Right**, as amended.
10. Skills text: README and SKILL.md now state D1's bucket 1 (objects, docs, capabilities) plus positions as the names that carry the namespace, every other name short, a prefixed name still valid, no `_`-led name; two eval `expected_output`s drop the prefix they asked for while their `must_contain` lists are unchanged, so a prefixed answer still passes (D9: nothing un-renames). `skills/**` nets −1 line (+6/−7). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `31669-behavioural-names-short-address-grammar.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/cli: patch`, `@objectstack/skills: patch`. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is a protocol kind, so spec takes at least `minor` under AGENTS.md step 3; cli and skills carry no protocol change, so `patch`. `@objectstack/skills` exists (`packages/skills/package.json`). The BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO remedy (`_sync` → `sync`, update every reference) and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`adr-0087: registered bucket-two-three-name-underscore-led-refused`) are present; semantic entry 18 exists at the head with that id, and `check-adr-0087-registration` sits inside the green repo-gates run. No `skip-changeset`. **Matches what the diff publishes.**
- The two declaration lines are line-initial and identical in the changeset and the PR body: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the title carries `!`. Claim amend 1's correction (`added` → `narrowed`, `yes` → `yes (narrowing)`) is what landed.
- **Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — right.** The one arm is the ten-schema `_` refusal; everything else the PR publishes is additive and unwired, and the lint change loosens a warning, which is not a contract.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — Acceptance note 1, the face hash (`ai/face-name.ts`).** Answered, accepted. (i) The algorithm is FNV-1a 32 as published: offset `0x811c9dc5`, prime `0x01000193`, xor-then-multiply, `Math.imul` followed by the unsigned-shift-by-zero coercion is the exact mod-2^32 product, 8 hex zero-padded. My probe gives `'' → 811c9dc5`, `'a' → e40c292c`, `'foobar' → bf9cf968` (the published vectors) and `c75940c6` for the 68-character face `crm_` + 51×`a` + `-convert_lead`, which is the literal the test pins. (ii) The input: "the UTF-8 bytes of the whole uncut face" satisfies the ruling's "a hash of the full identity": under D2 the address is `(namespace, name)` and the face IS that address spelled out; for `OBJECT-ACTION` the object name already carries the package (D6), and two holders of the same (object, action) are the face list's duplicate to refuse (D6 rider, G2/C), not the hash's to separate. Hashing the face, not a richer tuple, is also what lets G2 and the cloud derive the same name from the address they hold. Every grammar is `[a-z0-9_]`, so UTF-8 bytes equal code units; the TextEncoder spelling is still the right isomorphic one. (iii) `node:crypto` is unavailable in an isomorphic synchronous spec module; the tree already uses FNV-1a 32 in five isomorphic places (`service-settings` `crypto-adapter.ts` `fnv32:`, `service-messaging` `backoff.ts`, `types` `representation-validator.ts`, `metadata-core` `object-schema-fls.ts`, `platform-objects` `source-hash.ts`). (iv) The cut rule: a face of exactly 64 is not cut (ruling rider), a longer one is 55 + `-` + 8 = 64. Non-cryptographic is acceptable here because the hash only keeps two long faces with a shared 55-character head apart and the face list refuses a collision by name.
- **Acceptance note 2** (`os generate` still writes `NS_` scaffold names): accepted deviation under D9 (a kept spelling). It does mean the scaffolder writes a spelling the skills no longer teach; a follow-up card is the right place if the lane wants scaffolds short. Not a contract conflict.
- **Acceptance note 3** (the save door): verified. `protocol-save.ts` L1429 parses the item body against its type schema, so the schema refusal is reached at the save door too; the URL grammar (`METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN`, `saveMetaItem`/`publishMetaItem`) refuses a `_`-led name earlier with a message that does not name the router reservation. That message is metadata-protocol's, outside the card's surface; accepted as left.
- **Acceptance note 4** (environment object-bound action gets `OBJECT-ACTION`): right; D6 states the `OBJECT-ACTION` form "for an action bound to an object" without a holder condition, and the `NAME` form only under `NS-NAME`.
- **Acceptance note 5** (empty literal): verified at ledger L746; `''` fails `NAMESPACE_PATTERN` so it never enters the refused set; `readNamespacePositionSegment('actions', '')` reads it as a literal, which is the router's behaviour today.
- **Acceptance note 6** (nothing wired): the file list touches no runtime, objectql, mcp or metadata-protocol file.
- **Open questions**: ADR Q1, Q2, Q3 and D2 were ruled before this head and the PR body carries no `open_questions`; none to escalate.
- **The card's red lines.** (1) Resolution never loosens: nothing here resolves; `readNamespacePositionSegment` returns `bare` rather than a guess, admits `namespace` only when the segment passes the grammar AND the caller's catalogue says so, and its docblock says a bare reading is not a resolution. (2) Ambiguity reported: `findNamespaceObjectNameClashes` names both spellings and the package; `validateNamespaceNotAddressLiteral` names every door that serves the literal. (3) Independently releasable: (a) Test Core 1–8 and the Dogfood Regression Gate are green on the head; (b) no runtime file is touched, so bare-name behaviour is unchanged for every one-holder name, the declared narrowing excepted; (c) no migration; (d) the declarations and entry 18.
- **Dev deviations 1–5** are process; 3 (plain `git merge origin/main` twice) is covered by the regen family being green on this head. Accepted.
- **Devx notify (#31749)**: P exports no per-type bucket constant, so `scenario-naming.ts` has nothing to switch to; the card does not owe one. Left to a follow-up if wanted.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against:

- `kernel/address-grammar.ts` (D5): the door table matches D5's table; the three-step precedence matches D5 "How the router tells them apart" (literal, then `_env`, then installed namespace, else bare). The literal constant is complete against the ledger (①5). `validateNamespaceNotAddressLiteral` judges only the grammar and says so. Tried: `trigger` installed as a namespace on `/actions` reads as a namespace, on `/automation` as the literal (door-scoped, as D5 says); `Crm` with a lying catalogue reads bare; `_drafts` on `/automation` reads bare (it is a `/meta` type-position literal, not an automation one) — all as designed. One finding (F1).
- `ai/face-name.ts` (D6, Q1 = A): the three forms, the 64 boundary and the cut are the ruling's; `objectName || namespace` means an empty-string object falls through to the namespace, acceptable. Hash judged above. Exported from `ai/index.ts`; no import cycle (the module imports nothing).
- `ai/mcp.zod.ts` (D5 MCP bullet): declared once, mixed in by G2 as `confirm` is; docblock's absent/present/row semantics restate D3 and D5 without inventing a pick. Right.
- `kernel/namespace-prefix.ts` (Q3 = A, K): predicate semantics match the ruling; the second direction skips incoming namespaces already judged, so no clash is reported twice; an installed-vs-installed clash is correctly not this call's. Tried: a stack whose namespace equals one of its own objects → caught in direction 1 (incoming objects are in `allObjects`); an environment object `crm_custom` with no namespace is not the `custom` corollary (it belongs to no package) and is caught in direction 1 when the pair installs — right.
- `kernel/manifest.zod.ts`, `kernel/index.ts`, `ai/index.ts`: wiring only; message unchanged; no cycle (`address-grammar` imports nothing; `namespace-prefix` → `customization-package` → `manifest.zod` → `address-grammar`, acyclic).
- The ten schema files: one-line regex swaps with the shared message; the `describe` strings are unchanged, so the generated JSON schema changes only its `pattern`. Right.
- `migrations/entries/semantic/18.…ts`: surface, replacement, reason and acceptance match the tree (the ten schemas, the pattern, the three doors, the measured zero). Right.
- `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`: the replaced paragraph is true of the tree at this head sentence by sentence — the bucket-1 list is D1's, positions are D7's one slot, the lint sentence is exactly `PREFIX_JUDGED_COLLECTIONS` + `DUPLICATE_KEYED_TYPES`, "no name starts with `_`" is the ten-schema refusal plus `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` for the rest of the list. Against eval `config-plugins-ops` #1 the taught rule yields prefixed objects and short flows, and the unchanged `must_contain` still admits a prefixed flow. Right.
- `skills/README.md`: the convention line now matches SKILL.md's rule and points to it; the retired exemptions were exemptions to the retired rule. Right.
- The two eval files: `expected_output` only; assertions unchanged; `action_crm_escalate_case` is still the cloud's spelling on `main` (child C changes it, not P). Right.
- Implementing files: `lint.ts` agrees with D9 and with the SKILL.md sentence word for word (①6); the message now carries the collection's reason. `generate.ts` docblocks: true of `lint.ts` at this head. `doc-pages.mdx`: D1 restated correctly. The changeset: ②.

Findings:

- **F1 — nit** (`packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts`, module docblock and the `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS` docblock). Both say in the present tense that `route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` "pins this constant against the ledger rows so the two never drift". No such pin exists on this head: the only references to the constant outside its own file are the regenerated surface files, and the ADR's G1 row assigns that pin to G1. The values are correct today (①5), but drift is unguarded until G1 lands. No effect on correctness or the contract. Code face: leave as an accepted deviation to be made true by G1's pin, or a follow-up card; ⛔ not fixed on this head.
- **F2 — nit** (PR body, Acceptance note 1 and the spec bullet): "`face-name.test.ts` pins a literal value and the published vectors". The test pins the literal only; `fnv1a32Hex` is unexported, and the vectors appear in a comment. The probe verified them instead. Prose face; a one-word body correction is optional.
- **F3 — nit** (follow-up card at most): reference grammars wider than the names they reference — `agent.zod.ts` L386 `skills[]` and `skill.zod.ts` L375 `tools[]` still admit a `_`-led skill or tool name that no longer exists, and `api/metadata.zod.ts` L80 `MetadataRegisterRequestSchema.name` admits `_`-led (unreachable: the URL grammar refuses first). A `_`-led reference simply never resolves; no correctness or contract effect.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.

Adopted as rendered. F1 is carried to G1; F2 and F3 are accepted nits._
